desc:
A binary tree with pairwise distinct node values is described by two traversals: its preorder (node, left subtree, right subtree) and its postorder (left subtree, right subtree, node). The two arrays are guaranteed to be the preorder and the postorder of at least one binary tree.

Different trees can share both traversals. A node that has exactly one child may hold that child on its left or on its right, and the two traversals do not tell which. Count how many different binary trees (a left child and a right child are different things) have exactly this preorder and this postorder. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007. Two empty arrays describe the empty tree, which counts as one tree.

For preorder = [1, 2, 3] and postorder = [3, 2, 1] the tree is a chain 1 → 2 → 3 and each of the two links can go left or right: the answer is 4. For postorder = [2, 3, 1] the root has two children and the answer is 1.
constraints: The arrays are the preorder and postorder of at least one binary tree
hints: Consider one node and look at the traversals restricted to its subtree: where do its children show up in each array?

The first child of a node is the element right after it in the preorder; the last child is the element right before it in the postorder. If they are the same element, the node has a single child, which could be on either side.

If they differ, the node has two children and the split of the traversals is forced. So the answer is 2<sup>k</sup>, where k is the number of nodes with exactly one child. Detect them with a position table of the postorder.
editorial: Look at a node u with a non-empty subtree. In the preorder, the element after u is the root of its first child subtree, call it a (the left child if it exists, otherwise the right one). In the postorder, the element just before u is the root of the last child subtree, b (the right child if it exists, otherwise the left one). If u has two children then a is the left root and b the right root, and they differ. If u has one child both equal that child.

When a != b the structure below u is completely determined: the left subtree is the prefix of the preorder starting at a and the prefix of the postorder ending at a, which fixes its size. When a == b the single child can be attached on either side, giving a factor 2, and the rest of the structure is determined recursively. For a leaf the element after it in the preorder cannot be the element before it in the postorder (that node would have to be both a descendant of the leaf and not), so there is no false match.

Therefore the answer is 2k modulo 1,000,000,007 where k is the number of indices i with pos[preorder[i+1]] = pos[preorder[i]] - 1, pos being the index of a value in the postorder. One pass with a dictionary: O(n) time and space.
